targets.grammar: Build Schedules (the LIVE-tenant find/list grammar the scheduler click target actually boots at /workspace/scheduler/find): header + a three-counter tray whose two per-tick counters STATE their 15-second window + a Create-schedule typed absence · an N-schedules count band counted live from the records predicate, beside a Results-matching principal chip refused because the census is UNFILTERED · a sort / select / filter toolbar with the name-or-rid input, every one a typed absence with a reason written for it · the APPLICATIONS facet lane rendered as MISSING rather than the reference's own EMPTY · and the schedule table, served as a READ-ONLY PROJECTION over the estate's ONLY cadence records: automation records carrying a schedule_spec, read from /v1/hypervisor/automations because it is the COMPLETE projection (the pre-filtered Operations scheduler lane drops 24 fields including catch_up_policy, misfire_policy and executor_identity, recomputed field-by-field on every render). THE FINDING: the field NAMED for the concept is not the field the runtime acts on — the scheduler loop admits on `enabled && schedule_is_active(schedule_spec)` and never reads `trigger`, so the one automation it fires on a cron carries trigger_kind: manual, and a trigger-shaped view would have reported 0 schedules while the loop fired 1. Two published schedule counts come from two DIFFERENT predicates (Operations never reads `enabled`; the loop does) and their agreement is printed as a delta rather than assumed. The daemon's own posture says the loop dispatches through the MANUAL-RUN path, so no record marks a past run as scheduler-dispatched — the surface answers when a schedule WILL fire and refuses to say which past runs WERE fires. Fifteen schedule/cadence planes are classified live into FOUR states across THREE shapes (a collection, a status SINGLETON that is not a collection of one, a pure COMPUTATION that is not a plane at all). Read-only: the schedule verbs stay on Automations, the fires stay on Builds, loop health stays on Operations.

targets.grammar: HyperAuto (the LIVE-tenant card grammar the ingest click target actually boots at /workspace/hyperauto/pipeline): a header carrying the app name and its Create-pipeline typed absence · one centred card titled "HyperAuto Pipelines" repeating the same verb in its head · the card body, whose reference state is an EMPTY list carrying a badge, its own copy and a Go-to-Data-Connection-Application link — KEPT here as the honest rendering for an empty plane, and distinguished from the plane REFUSING the read · the APPLICATIONS facet lane rendered as MISSING rather than the reference's own EMPTY. Over that grammar the surface renders the estate's REAL ingestion CHAIN as a READ-ONLY projection: one row per connector-mapping record, joined END TO END on the keys the RECORDS carry — connector_mapping_id to the policy-bound data view, the transformation run, the ontology projection and the capability-lease plan; data_source_id to the materializing run; materializing_run_id to the connector session; and ontology_projection_id to the materialized object set, the ONLY mapping-keyed path to an output the estate publishes. Twenty-one ingestion-chain and adjacent planes are classified live into FOUR states (LIVE / EMPTY / REFUSED / NO READ ROUTE, the last decided from the daemon's own route index), each stamped with the STAGE it occupies so an adjacent plane is never read as a stage of the chain. THE FINDING: a self-report is scoped to the RECORD that carries it and never to the estate — a source whose rows were fetched under a receipted HTTP 200 still reads ingestion.wired:false (the flag is written once at declaration time and no run revises it); a mapping reads health.status:ready while the same object reports object_instances:0 and its own note says it extracts nothing; the plane roll-up states as a WHOLE-PLANE claim that nothing here moves source data, in an estate holding extracted rows that arrived through the lane beside it; missing_contracts names contracts that already exist for that very mapping because it is computed without reading downstream; and a connector session reports data_moved:false about the crossing its own object set names it as the provenance of. So no count is taken from a status field: three predicates are re-derived every render and each names itself — declared (a mapping exists), moved (source_contacted:true or an object set under the chain's own projection), rows (summed from the OUTPUT records, the only ones carrying a verbatim contact receipt) — and the session/run contradiction is NAMED rather than adjudicated. The automatic BUILDER is a typed absence counted from the route index: zero ODK routes accept a source and return a built chain, the path is thirteen separate authority-crossing POSTs confirmed against the index on render, and the nearest automatic lane (ontology-proposals) REFUSES this identity so unknown is printed as unknown, never as absent. Read-only: the chain verbs stay on Pipeline Builder and the Connections lease gate, the source plane and its Syncs lane stay on Data Connection, the extracted objects stay on the Object Explorer — all linked, none re-rendered.
